author: Nick Murray
description: The federal Liberal government voted to keep the B.C. coastal oil tanker ban in place Wednesday, defeating a Conservative bill that would have repealed it.
title: B.C. North Coast tanker ban to remain in place after Liberals vote down Tory bill

author: Jeremy Warren
description: The chief of Onion Lake Cree Nation says any attempt to reform, repeal or replace the 150-year-old federal Indian Act must be led by First Nations, not by Ottawa or Indigenous umbrella organizations.
title: First Nations must lead Indian Act reform, Onion Lake Cree Nation chief says

author: Arturo Chang
description: The federal government says a judge made several errors in a ruling that found it had a duty to provide some First Nations communities with adequate housing and safe drinking water.
title: Canada 'not a bystander' on First Nations' housing, water issues, lawyer says in class-action appeal

author: Bill Graveland
description: An innovative wound and burn treatment initially funded by Canada's Department of National Defence is now being delivered by drone to help wounded soldiers and civilians in war-torn Ukraine.
title: Calgary-developed wound treatment used on battlefields in Ukraine

author: Vincent McDermott
description: Insp. Wayne Stevenson of the RCMP’s serious crime branch said at a news conference Wednesday in Edmonton that Fiasal "was associated with people involved in criminality" and knew the three accused. Stevenson alleged that Fiasal was lured from his home before being killed.
title: Three face murder charges in death of 12-year-old boy found in rural Alberta

author: Sarah Law
description: Indigenous leaders in Ontario are urging the provincial and federal governments to take action address what they call an infrastructure crisis at remote airports across the north. Nishnawbe Aski Nation and Chiefs of Ontario held a joint news conference in Toronto on Wednesday afternoon after launching a documentary and advocacy campaign to address the issue. According to a high-level needs assessment conducted by NAN last year, addressing infrastructure deficiencies across these airports would cost up to $1.5 billion.
title: First Nation chiefs urge Ontario, federal governments to address infrastructure crisis at remote airports

description: Frank Stronach's lawyer says one charge of sexual assault against her client in an upcoming Newmarket, Ont., trial has been dropped.
title: 1 charge dropped ahead of second Frank Stronach sexual assault trial: lawyer

author: Ryan Cooke
description: Newfoundland and Labrador's justice minister says a shipment of 1,200 toothbrushes was set to arrive at Her Majesty's Penitentiary on Tuesday. The mother of an inmate who went without one since early October says the shortage deprived her son of basic human dignity.
title: Mother of inmate at N.L.'s largest jail says toothbrush shortage was unacceptable

description: The leader of Alberta's Opposition NDP says Premier Danielle Smith's governing United Conservatives are cooking the riding boundaries for their own advantage ahead of next year's election.
title: Alberta NDP says Smith's UCP cooking riding boundaries for own benefit

author: Nicole Brockbank
description: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski addressed the jury for the first time at his Toronto fraud trial, thanking them, in his brief closing statement Wednesday morning.
title: 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski addresses jury at his fraud trial for first time, says he's innocent

author: Joel Dryden
description: The United Conservative Party government will press ahead with its plan to opt out of federal dental and drug benefit programs in favour of its own made-in-Alberta approach, even though voters rejected a similar strategy in last week's referendum.
title: Alberta pursuing own dental, drug plans despite referendum defeat on federal opt-outs

author: Matthew Lapierre
description: Jimmy Ylimaki, a Montreal man accused of defrauding American seniors as part of an elaborate grandparent scam network, has pleaded guilty in a U.S. court.
title: Montreal grandparent scammer who fled to Central America pleads guilty in U.S. court

description: On the eve of the Canada-EU summit in Montreal, Prime Minister Mark Carney and Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon are each urging the other to rethink their stances on Quebec's role at the event.
title: Quebec premier wants Carney to 'do the right thing,' let him speak at Canada-EU summit

author: Catharine Tunney, Kate McKenna, Marina von Stackelberg
description: A joint Canada-EU statement expected to be released on Friday is dropping the title of associate member and will instead use softer language promising closer ties, according to sources who have seen the latest draft of the statement.
title: EU dropping associate membership title for its closer alliance with Canada: sources

author: Peter Zimonjic
description: Canada's industry minister says she called the department's lawyers after the head of Stelco's American parent company told CBC News that he only bought the Hamilton steelmaker to stop it undercutting his production facilities in the U.S.
title: U.S. steel CEO's 'confessions' for buying Stelco prompted government to call its lawyers: industry minister

author: Alex Flood
description: Sault Ste. Marie MPP Chris Scott has been sitting at Queen's Park as an Independent since being arrested for spousal assault and assault with a weapon in September last year.
title: Sault Ste. Marie MPP Chris Scott 'grateful' for charges being withdrawn

author: Leah Hendry, Benjamin Shingler
description: Students and professors are raising questions about how McGill University handled the admission of a convicted murderer to its law school this fall, as authorities evaluate whether he will remain behind bars.
title: McGill law controversy exposes gaps in how universities handle students with criminal records
Bank of Canada expected to hike interest rate 25 points as inflation ticks upward

author: Jeff Lagerquist
description: A poll of 50 CEOs of large Canadian companies shows nearly half are eyeing smaller, more productive workforces with the help of AI.
title: 46% of Canadian CEOs eyeing AI-driven growth with smaller staff, poll shows

author: Katie Teeling
description: A massive data centre proposed in west-central Alberta is raising questions from area residents, who crowded into a recent series of information sessions hosted by Tourmaline Oil Corporation, the company behind the project.
title: Proposed data centre in west-central Alberta prompts pushback from some residents, support from others

author: Jacqueline Newsome
description: The PQ intend to table a bill in the coming months, and hear from experts in a parliamentary committee.
title: Parti Québécois promises to abolish time change, starting next year

author: Talia Kliot
description: The prizes recognize the best Canadian books in seven categories, from fiction to kids books.
title: Canisia Lubrin, David A. Robertson and Miriam Toews shortlisted for $25K Governor General's Literary Awards

author: Andrew Jeffrey
description: Canadian oil is typically sold at a discount compared to the North American benchmark, but that gap has widened in recent months with no clear short-term solution in sight.
title: Oil trading in triple digits, but Canadian crude selling at steeper discount

author: Aliyah Marko-Omene
description: Marina Hills and Sergio Losco are working to keep their son Henry's legacy alive as a law named after him is set to come into effect in Saskatchewan on Nov. 1. The 11-year-old died as a result of a carbon monoxide leak after a boiler malfunction in the Metro 1827 apartment building in downtown Regina last December.
title: Parents of boy who died in Regina apartment say new CO detector law honours his legacy

author: Ian Froese
description: A Manitoba man battling a degenerative disease won't lose access to his life-sustaining drug, with the province now promising coverage after a federal agency reversed its recommendation against its use in adults over 25.
title: Manitoba man won't lose access to drug slowing degenerative disease's progression after federal shift

description: Today is municipal election day for most of Manitoba. Voting locations will be open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
title: Manitobans head to polls today for general municipal election

author: Shawn Jeffords
description: The chairs of eight regional governments across the province will be appointed by Premier Doug Ford’s government within weeks, says Ontario’s municipal affairs minister, as opposition parties express concern the hand-picked leaders will be partisan appointees.
title: Ontario will appoint hand-picked regional chairs within weeks. Critics call the move 'undemocratic'

author: Steve Rukavina
description: Ten students at a high school in Lévis, Que., have been suspended after several AI-altered images of teachers and school staff were posted to Snapchat. Experts say both teachers and students need more education about the risks of AI and online images.
title: 10 students suspended at Lévis, Que., high school for posting AI-altered images of staff

author: David Thurton
description: Canada is facing a carbon tariff threat from the European Union within months as the economic bloc fully implements its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism.
title: Canada facing carbon tariff threat from European Union: internal documents

description: As winter approaches, people experiencing homelessness are building makeshift cabins — some equipped with generators and solar panels. It's a trend that's cropping up amid plans from the City of Montreal to address the growing need for affordable housing at an upcoming homelessness summit.
title: Encampment structures in Montreal raise safety concerns, but options are running out as winter nears

author: Mercedes Gaztambide
description: Waymo's plan to bring driverless ride-hailing vehicles to Canada has some drivers and advocates concerned the market is about to get more crowded and that more rideshare and taxi drivers could find themselves out of work.
title: How Waymo could push Toronto taxi and Uber drivers off the road

author: Brett Forester
description: University of Ottawa's president is acknowledging "a failure of the university" as Indigenous academics go public with allegations that a difficult work environment, poor treatment and racism at uOttawa and a lack of effort to address those problems has led multiple promising Indigenous scholars to quit.
title: Indigenous scholars allege racism, poor treatment at University of Ottawa
